questions.question:
Namespace `ticketing` has accumulated Secrets over several fare-system migrations. Take stock without deleting anything.

- Find every Secret of type `Opaque` in namespace `ticketing` that is **not referenced by any Pod** in that namespace. A Secret counts as referenced when a Pod uses it through `env` (`secretKeyRef`), `envFrom` or a volume (including projected volumes) of any of its containers or init containers.
- Write the names of those Secrets to `/home/candidate/exam/q1/orphaned-secrets.txt`, one name per line, sorted alphabetically.
- Label exactly those Secrets with `lifecycle=orphaned`. When you are done, no other Secret in the namespace may carry that label.
- Do not delete or modify any Pod, and do not change Secrets other than their labels.

verification.description: orphaned-secrets.txt lists exactly the unreferenced Opaque Secrets, sorted
Exactly those Secrets carry lifecycle=orphaned (no other Secret has the label)

questions.question:
Namespace `junction` runs a blue/green pair behind Service `junction`: `junction-blue` is live and `junction-green` is the new release, which has not been started yet. Cut the traffic over to green:

- Before changing anything, write the current selector of Service `junction` to `/home/candidate/exam/q2/old-selector.txt` as `key=value` pairs sorted by key and joined with commas (format: `k1=v1,k2=v2`).
- Scale `junction-green` to the number of replicas `junction-blue` runs now. All of them must be Ready.
- Point Service `junction` at the green Pods by changing only the value of its `slot` selector key. Do not modify the Service's `ports`. When you are done, the endpoints of `junction` must be exactly the `junction-green` Pods, on port 80.
- Scale `junction-blue` to 0 replicas. Do not delete it.

Verify with: `kubectl -n junction get endpoints junction -o wide`

verification.description: old-selector.txt holds the previous selector app=junction,slot=blue,tier=web
junction-green runs 4 Ready replicas (the size of blue) and keeps nginx:1.26
Service selector is app=junction,slot=green,tier=web, ports unchanged, endpoints are exactly the junction-green Pods on port 80
junction-blue still exists with 0 replicas and no blue Pods running

questions.question:
Namespace `helmyard` contains several Helm releases of the local chart `depot-web`. Both packaged versions of the chart are in `/home/candidate/exam/q3/`: `depot-web-0.1.0.tgz` and `depot-web-0.2.0.tgz`. The chart names its Deployment after the release.

- One release in `helmyard` is currently in status `failed`. Write its name to `/home/candidate/exam/q3/failed-release.txt`.
- Repair that release with `helm upgrade` (do not uninstall it): it must become `deployed` with its Pods running `nginx:1.26`, stay on chart version `0.1.0` and keep all of its other user-supplied values.
- Upgrade release `route-planner` to chart version `0.2.0`. Its user-supplied values must stay exactly as they are now, and everything it does not override must come from the 0.2.0 chart defaults (0.2.0 defaults to `nginx:1.26` and adds the ConfigMap `route-planner-board`).
- The Deployments of both releases must end up with all replicas Ready.

Verify with: `helm -n helmyard ls -a`, `helm -n helmyard history <release>`, `helm -n helmyard get values <release>`

verification.description: failed-release.txt names the release that is in status failed (stop-indexer)
stop-indexer repaired by an upgrade: original failed revision kept, now deployed on depot-web-0.1.0 with image.tag 1.26 and its other user values
Deployment stop-indexer has 3/3 Ready replicas on nginx:1.26 with label lane=local
route-planner upgraded to depot-web-0.2.0 (deployed) with exactly its original user-supplied values
route-planner runs the 0.2.0 defaults (nginx:1.26, ConfigMap route-planner-board) with its custom values, 2/2 Ready

questions.question:
The Pods of Deployment `wagon-sorter` in namespace `depot` never start.

- Find out why and fix the Deployment so that all `3` replicas run on the depot node (the node labeled `transit.io/pool=depot`) and can never be scheduled onto any other node.
- Do not modify any node (labels and taints stay as they are) and do not use `nodeName`.
- Write the name of the depot node to `/home/candidate/exam/q4/depot-node.txt`.

Verify with: `kubectl -n depot get pods -o wide`

verification.description: depot-node.txt contains the name of the depot node
wagon-sorter tolerates dedicated=depot:NoSchedule and its node selection matches only the depot node (no nodeName)
3/3 wagon-sorter Pods Running and Ready on the depot node; node taint and labels unchanged

questions.question:
In namespace `sleepers`, the Pods of one Deployment never become Ready: the kubelet keeps restarting one of their containers because its liveness probe fails while the application is still starting up (it needs about 40 seconds before it answers HTTP).

- Find that Deployment and write its name to `/home/candidate/exam/q5/deployment.txt`.
- Add a `startupProbe` to the affected container: the same HTTP check as its livenessProbe, `periodSeconds: 5`, no initial delay, and a `failureThreshold` that gives the container exactly 60 seconds to start.
- Do not change the existing livenessProbe and readinessProbe, the images or the commands.
- After the rollout, both replicas must be Ready and all containers of the new Pods must have a restart count of `0`.

verification.description: deployment.txt names the Deployment killed by its liveness probe (sleeper-berths)
container warmer has a startupProbe GET / on port http, periodSeconds 5, no initial delay, failureThreshold 12
livenessProbe, readinessProbe, images and commands of sleeper-berths unchanged
rollout complete: 2 current Pods Running and Ready with restartCount 0

questions.question:
The Pods of Deployment `claims-desk` in namespace `lostproperty` never start. The approved settings for the desk are listed in `/home/candidate/exam/q6/desk-settings.properties`.

- Write the exact waiting reason reported for the failing containers to `/home/candidate/exam/q6/reason.txt`.
- Fix the problem only by adding the missing key(s) to ConfigMap `desk-config`, with the approved values. Add exactly the keys whose absence stops a container from starting, nothing else, and do not change the existing keys.
- Do not edit, scale, restart or re-create the Deployment. Both replicas must end up Running with all containers Ready.

verification.description: reason.txt contains CreateContainerConfigError
desk-config has claim.window=45d and ledger.path=/var/ledger/claims.db; existing keys unchanged
No other keys were added to desk-config (the optional notify.webhook stays absent)
Deployment claims-desk is the original object, unmodified (generation 1), with 2 Ready Pods

questions.question:
In namespace `fares`, Deployment `fare-board` publishes two files from ConfigMap `fare-table`: `/usr/share/nginx/html/fares/current.txt` (key `peak.txt`) and `/usr/share/nginx/html/fares/offpeak.txt` (key `offpeak.txt`). The ConfigMap was updated a while ago, but the running Pods still show the old fares.

- Change `fare-board` so that future ConfigMap changes reach running Pods without a restart: mount one `fare-table` volume as the directory `/usr/share/nginx/html/fares` (no `subPath`), keeping both file paths and the keys they come from. The directory must contain only `current.txt` and `offpeak.txt`.
- Leave the rest of the Pod (image, ports, the `style` mount) unchanged.
- When the new Pods are Running, set key `peak.txt` of `fare-table` to `PEAK 3.95` and leave the other keys as they are. Do not restart, delete or re-create the Pods after this change: the running Pods must show the new value by themselves (the kubelet can take up to 1-2 minutes).

Verify with: `kubectl -n fares exec deploy/fare-board -- cat /usr/share/nginx/html/fares/current.txt`

verification.description: fare-table is mounted once as directory /usr/share/nginx/html/fares with items peak.txt->current.txt and offpeak.txt->offpeak.txt, no subPath
a current Pod shows only current.txt and offpeak.txt in the directory, index.html and the style mount are intact
fare-table peak.txt is PEAK 3.95, offpeak.txt and night.txt unchanged
Pods created before the ConfigMap change serve PEAK 3.95 in current.txt (not re-created)

questions.question:
Create Pod `signal-box` in namespace `signals`. Its configuration file is rendered at start-up from the template in ConfigMap `box-template` (key `box.conf.tpl`).

- Main container `box`: image `nginx:1.25`, CPU limit `250m`. It mounts an `emptyDir` volume at `/etc/signal` and must find the rendered file at `/etc/signal/box.conf`.
- Init container `render`: image `busybox:1.36`. It writes `box.conf` into that volume from the template, replacing every `%POD_NAME%` with the Pod's name, every `%NODE_NAME%` with the name of the node the Pod runs on, and every `%CPU_LIMIT%` with the CPU limit of container `box` in millicores. All other template content stays unchanged.
- The three values must reach `render` as environment variables from the downward API; do not hard-code them.

Verify with: `kubectl -n signals exec signal-box -c box -- cat /etc/signal/box.conf`

verification.description: signal-box: init container render (busybox:1.36) completed; box (nginx:1.25, CPU limit 250m) Ready
render gets metadata.name, spec.nodeName and box's limits.cpu (divisor 1m) from the downward API
/etc/signal/box.conf in box is the fully rendered template (real Pod name, node name, 250)
exit-code.txt contains 23 (exit code of the verify-feed init container)
timetable-build: completions 6, parallelism 3, Indexed, backoffLimit 2, activeDeadlineSeconds 240, ttlSecondsAfterFinished 86400, busybox:1.36
timetable-build is Complete with 6 succeeded Pods
Each completion index 0-5 logged 'timetable shard <index> built'

questions.question:
Namespace `yardsafety` enforces the `restricted` Pod Security Standard. Deployment `shunter` should run 2 replicas but has no Pods at all.

- Find out why, and fix the Pod template of `shunter` so that both replicas are created and become Running and Ready.
- Do not change the namespace's labels. Keep the images, commands and container names (init container `prep`, container `shunter`), and keep volume `scratch` mounted at `/scratch` in both containers.
- The `scratch` volume must use a volume type the policy allows: make it an `emptyDir`.
- Do not run anything privileged and do not add any Linux capabilities.

verification.description: namespace still enforces restricted (labels unchanged) and a Pod built from the shunter template is admitted (server dry-run)
prep and shunter set allowPrivilegeEscalation=false, drop ALL capabilities and add none
every container runs with runAsNonRoot=true, a non-zero runAsUser and seccomp RuntimeDefault
scratch is an emptyDir mounted at /scratch in both containers; images and commands unchanged
shunter has 2/2 Ready Pods, init container prep completed

questions.question:
Workloads in namespace `permits` will pull images from a private registry.

- Create a docker-registry Secret `permits-registry` for server `registry.permits.transit.local:5443`, username `permit-bot` and password `Gr33n$ignal-7`.
- Make the namespace's `default` ServiceAccount use `permits-registry` as an image pull secret, in addition to the pull secret it already has.
- Create a TLS Secret `permits-tls` from the certificate `/home/candidate/exam/q11/certs/gate.crt` and its private key. The key is one of the files in `/home/candidate/exam/q11/certs/keys/`.
- The existing Pod `permit-check` must end up with both pull secrets of the `default` ServiceAccount in its spec. It must receive them from the ServiceAccount: do not list `imagePullSecrets` in the Pod yourself. Keep its name, its image `registry.k8s.io/pause:3.9` and its ServiceAccount; it must be Running.

verification.description: permits-registry is a dockerconfigjson Secret with the exact server, username and password
ServiceAccount default lists permits-registry and still lists legacy-pull

questions.question:
The source of the dispatch board image is in `/home/candidate/exam/q12/app`. A container registry is running at `localhost:5000`.

- Build the image `localhost:5000/dispatch-board:2.3` from that directory with the build arguments `DISPATCH_ZONE=riverside` and `BUILD_NO=417`, and push it to the registry. The pushed image must carry the labels `transit.dispatch/zone=riverside` and `transit.dispatch/build=417`, and its page must show `zone=riverside build=417`. You may edit the Dockerfile, but keep its base image.
- Write only the value of the image's label `transit.dispatch/release`, as reported by `docker image inspect`, to `/home/candidate/exam/q12/release.txt`.
- Create Deployment `dispatch-board` in namespace `dispatch` with `2` replicas and one container named `board` running image `localhost:5000/dispatch-board:2.3`. Both Pods must be Ready and serve the new page (`/usr/share/nginx/html/index.html`).

verification.description: Registry holds dispatch-board:2.3 with labels zone=riverside, build=417, release=riverside-417
release.txt holds the value of label transit.dispatch/release
Deployment dispatch-board: container board runs localhost:5000/dispatch-board:2.3 with 2/2 ready replicas
Every ready dispatch-board Pod serves zone=riverside build=417

questions.question:
The Pods of Deployment `load-planner` in namespace `capacity` stay `Pending`. Other Pods in the namespace are Pending for their own reasons: leave them alone.

- Find the container of `load-planner` whose resource request the scheduler cannot satisfy, and the resource concerned. Write them to `/home/candidate/exam/q13/blocker.txt` as `<container>:<resource>`.
- Change only that container, so that it has exactly: requests `cpu: 50m`, `memory: 96Mi`; limits `cpu: 100m`, `memory: 128Mi`. The other container and the other workloads must not change.
- All 3 replicas of `load-planner` must be Running and Ready.

verification.description: blocker.txt contains cache:memory
Only the cache container changed: requests cpu 50m / memory 96Mi, limits cpu 100m / memory 128Mi; planner container and load-reporter unchanged
load-planner keeps 3 replicas, all updated, scheduled and Ready

questions.question:
The platform display boards in namespace `platform` must be published through the Traefik ingress controller.

- Create Ingress `platform-board` with ingress class `traefik` for host `board.transit.local`: path `/departures` (pathType `Prefix`) must reach the Pods of Deployment `departures-web`, and path `/arrivals` (pathType `Prefix`) the Pods of Deployment `arrivals-web`. Use the existing Services that select those Pods; do not create or modify Services.
- From a temporary Pod, request `http://traefik.kube-system/departures/next` and `http://traefik.kube-system/arrivals/next` with the header `Host: board.transit.local`, and save the response bodies to `/home/candidate/exam/q14/departures.out` and `/home/candidate/exam/q14/arrivals.out`.

verification.description: Ingress platform-board uses ingressClassName traefik and host board.transit.local
/departures -> departures:80 and /arrivals -> arrivals-live:8081 (number or name), both Prefix
departures.out is the departures-web response for /departures/next served through Traefik
arrivals.out is the arrivals-web (not legacy) response for /arrivals/next served through Traefik

questions.question:
The CRD `routes.transit.example.com` (kind `Route`) is installed. Note that another API group in the cluster also serves a resource named `routes`.

- In namespace `manifests`, create two `Route` objects of API group `transit.example.com`, using the field names and codes documented in the CRD's schema (`kubectl explain`):
  - `f1-islands`: line `F1`, mode `ferry`, `6` stops, depot `pier-2`, a local all-stops service, one departure every `30` minutes.
  - `n9-nightliner`: line `N9`, mode `bus`, `31` stops, depot `north`, part of the night network, one departure every `20` minutes.
- Write a listing of all `transit.example.com` Routes in namespace `manifests` to `/home/candidate/exam/q15/routes.txt`: no header line, one Route per line with four whitespace-separated columns (name, line, service class code, number of stops), sorted by number of stops, ascending.

verification.description: Route f1-islands (transit.example.com) has line F1, mode ferry, stops 6, depot pier-2, serviceClass C1, frequencyMinutes 30
Route n9-nightliner (transit.example.com) has line N9, mode bus, stops 31, depot north, serviceClass C5, frequencyMinutes 20
routes.txt lists all 7 transit Routes (name line serviceClass stops, no header) sorted by stops and matches the live objects

questions.question:
Kustomize files for the route board are in `/home/candidate/exam/q16`: a `base/` and an example overlay `overlays/staging/`, which is already applied in namespace `routes`. Create the overlay `overlays/prod/` and apply it with `kubectl apply -k`:

- It builds on `../../base`, puts everything in namespace `routes` and prefixes all names with `prod-`.
- Label every resource `env=prod`. The prod Deployment and Service must select only prod Pods; the namespace also runs other Pods labelled `app=route-board`.
- The Deployment runs 3 replicas and its `web` container uses `nginx:1.26` (the other container is unchanged).
- The generated ConfigMap keeps all base keys, except that `ROUTE_MODE` becomes `express`, and it gains `NIGHT_SERVICE=enabled`. Extend the base generator (merge) instead of redefining it.
- Do not modify `base/` or `overlays/staging/`.

Verify with: `kubectl -n routes get endpoints prod-route-board`

verification.description: overlays/prod renders, builds on ../../base, and base/ and overlays/staging/ are unchanged
Deployment prod-route-board: selector app=route-board,env=prod, 3 Ready replicas, web nginx:1.26, feed-sync busybox:1.36
The Deployment uses the rendered prod-route-settings-<hash> ConfigMap with the merged data (behavior: merge)
Service prod-route-board selects app=route-board,env=prod and its endpoints are exactly the 3 prod Pods

questions.question:
Deployment `kiosk` in namespace `kiosk` serves HTTP on TCP port `80`; its `metrics` sidecar listens on TCP `8081`. Restrict who can reach the kiosk Pods:

- Create NetworkPolicy `kiosk-ingress` in namespace `kiosk` that applies to the Pods of Deployment `kiosk` only.
- Allow ingress only from Pods labeled `role=monitor` that run in a namespace labeled `team=ops` (both conditions at once), and from any Pod in namespace `kiosk`.
- From either source only TCP port `80` may be reached; all other ingress to the kiosk Pods, including port `8081`, must be denied. Policies that already exist in `kiosk` must not allow more than this.
- Do not change any namespace or Pod labels.

Test from the Pods `monitor` and `guest` in namespaces `ops-east` and `ops-west` and from Pod `kiosk-client`, e.g. `kubectl -n ops-east exec monitor -- wget -qO- -T 2 http://<kiosk-pod-ip>`

verification.description: kiosk-ingress exists, has type Ingress and selects the kiosk Pods only (not kiosk-cache or kiosk-client)
all policies selecting the kiosk Pods together allow TCP 80 only from role=monitor in team=ops namespaces and from namespace kiosk, and never 8081 (Pod and namespace labels unchanged)
live: ops-east/monitor reaches kiosk:80, ops-east/guest and ops-west/monitor are blocked
live: kiosk-client reaches kiosk:80, port 8081 is blocked from kiosk-client and ops-east/monitor

questions.question:
Deployment `freight-api` in namespace `freight` must run with its own read-only identity.

- Create ServiceAccount `freight-reader`, a Role `freight-reader` and a RoleBinding `freight-reader` that grant it `get`, `list` and `watch` on ConfigMaps and `get` on the Secret `route-key` only. In namespace `freight` the ServiceAccount must end up with no permissions beyond these; do not change what any other subject is allowed to do.
- Make `freight-api` run as `freight-reader`, with the ServiceAccount token mounted into its Pods.
- Write the output of these three commands, in this order, one per line, to `/home/candidate/exam/q18/can-i.txt`:
  - `kubectl auth can-i watch configmaps -n freight --as=system:serviceaccount:freight:freight-reader`
  - `kubectl auth can-i get secret/route-key -n freight --as=system:serviceaccount:freight:freight-reader`
  - `kubectl auth can-i get secret/tariff-db -n freight --as=system:serviceaccount:freight:freight-reader`

Verify with: `kubectl auth can-i --list -n freight --as=system:serviceaccount:freight:freight-reader`

verification.description: ServiceAccount, Role and RoleBinding freight-reader exist and are bound together
freight-reader can get/list/watch ConfigMaps and get only Secret route-key, nothing more
Pre-existing edit grant no longer reaches freight-reader; yardmaster and freight-writer keep their access
freight-api Pods run as freight-reader with the API token mounted
can-i.txt holds yes / yes / no
